question: In January, a number of official letters were sent to the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Türkiye, with copies to the Turkish Embassy in the European Union, to request authorisation to visit Mayor of Istanbul Ekrem İmamoğlu, who has been imprisoned on patently unfounded charges. Despite several reminders, no answer has been provided.

This raises serious concerns about Türkiye’s compliance with its rule of law obligations, procedural safeguards, the rights of detained people and democratic pluralism, even though it remains a candidate country for EU membership and is a member of the Council of Europe. 1.
What action does the Commission intend to take with the Turkish authorities to obtain a formal response to requests to visit Mr İmamoğlu in prison?

In the view of the Commission and the European External Action Service, is the lack of response from the Turkish authorities and the detention of Mr İmamoğlu compatible with Türkiye’s commitments as an EU candidate country?
Does the Commission intend to draw political conclusions from this situation concerning its relations with Türkiye?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.8.2026) The Commission is concerned about developments in Türkiye regarding the rule of law and the protection of fundamental rights. These concerns include the detention of Ekrem İmamoğlu1, as outlined in the 2025 enlargement report2.

As an EU candidate country and long-standing member of the Council of Europe, Türkiye is expected to apply the highest democratic standards and practices. The Commission will continue to promote these values in its relations with Türkiye and to address these issues in all relevant contacts with the Turkish authorities, including in the relevant subcommittee established under the Association Agreement with Türkiye3.

Since the end of 2024, the Turkish authorities have authorised several prison visits for the Türkiye rapporteur in the European Parliament and for the chair of the European Parliament’s Subcommittee on Human Rights. The Commission will raise the lack of response to some requests in future meetings and dialogues with Turkish officials.

The criteria allowing or restricting such visits should reflect the requirements of Article 8 of the European Convention on Human Rights4 and of the Optional Protocol to the Convention against Torture. Difficulties in gaining access to inmates persist and in recent cases, the European Court of Human Rights5 has ruled that Türkiye violated prisoners’ rights regarding visits and telephone calls at weekends.
Respect for fundamental rights and the rule of law are essential for the EU accession process. They will continue to be an integral part of EU-Türkiye relations.
